expectations.text: Flags the nested comments and attachments resolvers as unscoped by tenant
expectations.evidence: Document.comments and Document.attachments filter by documentId only. That's safe only if the parent was always obtained through getDocument

expectations.text: Flags updateDocument for scoping on id alone without a tenant constraint
expectations.evidence: where: { id: documentId } with no tenantId. Tenant A can overwrite the title/body of any document whose ID they know

expectations.text: Flags exportWorkspace taking tenantId from the client-controlled request body
expectations.evidence: tenantId comes from req.body, not the session — client-controlled, so it's a one-line dump

expectations.text: Flags searchDocuments as returning rows across all tenants
expectations.evidence: session is accepted and never used. Full-text search runs across every tenant's documents

expectations.text: Flags adminListDocuments as checking authentication but not authorization or tenant
expectations.evidence: Only checks the user is authenticated (not that they're an admin), then returns the 200 most recent documents across all tenants

expectations.text: Enumerates all the affected sites rather than fixing only the first one found
expectations.evidence: Lists 1-5 as problems (updateDocument, exportWorkspace, searchDocuments, adminListDocuments, nested resolvers), item 6 notes getDocument is fine

expectations.text: Recommends a structural device (scoped repository, row-level security, or equivalent) rather than only adding where-clauses site by site
expectations.evidence: Postgres RLS with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and app.tenant_id set per-transaction... A TenantDb constructed only from a session, with the raw db lint-banned

expectations.text: Recommends a cross-tenant test that attempts tenant A operations against tenant B resources
expectations.evidence: The two-tenant test: table-drive every operation from tenant A against tenant B's IDs, assert 404 (not 403)

expectations.text: Identifies the raw interpolation of tenantId into $queryRawUnsafe as an injection hazard distinct in kind from the tenant-scoping bug
expectations.evidence: And it's string-interpolated into $queryRawUnsafe, so '; DROP ... works too. Two breaches in one function

expectations.text: Does not conclude the main query paths being scoped means the service is safe
expectations.evidence: the obvious path is scoped, which is why a spot check says 'we're ok.' [implicit criticism]. Why per-site fixes aren't enough
